title: Definition record
description: A defined term as one instrument defines it. SCHEMA.md § 2: "personal information" means five different things across FCRA, GLBA, HIPAA, COPPA and NY SHIELD, and differs_from is where a lot of the expert value lives. That value is only real if the difference is CHECKABLE, so a definition is decomposed into elements tagged with concepts from meta/definition-concepts.yaml, and differs_from is COMPUTED from those element sets by tools/compute-differs.mjs and re-verified by gate 26. A hand-written difference is an assertion nothing checks.

position.description: Context is bidirectional. USLM <continuation> puts the operative consequence AFTER the enumerated list — the chapeau is the 'if' and the continuation is the 'then'. 468 instances in title 15 alone.

relation_note.description: Required when relation is 'other'. A missing enum value should be a recorded gap, not a silent mis-fit.

verbatim_span.description: Context is quoted law, not annotation. Gate 3 verifies it in its own right.

paragraph_path.description:
Where this text sits in the enacted hierarchy. In USLM the path is READ from identifier attributes; in eCFR it is RECONSTRUCTED from designators parsed out of flat

siblings, because eCFR carries no element nesting below the section. Same field, incomparable reliability — which is why derivation is recorded rather than assumed.

path.description: Designators outermost-first, relative to the section: subsection (a) is ["a"], (a)(6)(A) is ["a","6","A"]. An EMPTY array is the section root itself, which is what a section-level chapeau has — see DEBT-005. minItems is 0 for exactly that reason.

anchor.description: The source's own element identifier, where it has one (USLM identifier=, eCFR N=). Gate 17 checks this against the non-operative regions of the source.

derivation.description: structural = transcribed from a publisher assertion. reconstructed = inferred by this repo from designator text; eCFR only.

confidence.description: structural is always high. reconstructed is low wherever a designator's level is ambiguous in context — the eCFR (i) case, where (i) is both letter-nine and roman-one. Low REFUSES the atom (gate 16).

evidence.description: How the path was determined. For structural, the attribute and element type. For reconstructed, the sequence reasoning.

text_file.description: Deterministic text rendering of raw_file, for binary sources (PDF). Gate 3 checks verbatim_span against this when present.

format.description: How the primary text was obtained. Structured formats are a HARD preference: a PDF is a rendering of a document, and every transformation of a rendering is a place a quotation can silently drift. See risk_tier.

risk_tier.description: Derived from format: xml/json/html low, pdf_single_col medium, pdf_multi_col high, manual high. CI recomputes it; a mismatch is a gate-1 failure. High tier triggers gate 12 sampling.

structured_source_check.description: Recorded result of looking for a structured source BEFORE falling back to PDF. A negative result is a finding worth keeping — it stops the next session repeating the search.

render.description: Structured render parameters. Present for pdf_* sources so gate 11 can drive an INDEPENDENT renderer with identical parameters. Kept structured rather than parsed back out of text_extraction_cmd, which would be fragile.

segment_sha256.description: sha256 of the SEGMENTATION LEAF this record is anchored to, normalised for whitespace. Not the raw file — raw_sha256 already covers that, and it does not move when a WALKER changes. This does. A walker fix re-cuts the leaves under every atom over that source, and an atom whose leaf was re-cut is no longer verified against the thing it quotes: N.Y. Penal Law s 250.00 welded subdivisions 1 and 2 into one leaf, and the atom quoting it cited s 250.00(1) while carrying the words of s 250.00(2). Gate 38 compares this against the current segmentation. null means not yet baselined and is skipped with a declared reason.

source_defects.description: Errors in the source AS PUBLISHED. as_published and apparent_intent are separate keys on purpose: it is structurally impossible for a correction to leak into verbatim_span.

apparent_intent.description: INFERENCE. Labelled as such. Never authoritative, never substituted for the text.

span_interruptions.description: Apparatus that interrupts the operative text mid-span, recorded rather than silently deleted. Each entry is an offset into verbatim_span, the exact excluded characters, and what kind of apparatus it is. CI gate 3 REBUILDS the raw substring by re-inserting every entry at its offset and requires the result to appear in the source. That makes the removal mechanically reversible: the operative words cannot be edited without breaking reconstruction. Prefer choosing span boundaries that avoid apparatus. Use this only where operative text is unavoidably interrupted, because splitting the span would lose the fact that it is one sentence.

offset.description: Character index into verbatim_span at which the excluded text sat.

excluded_text.description: Exact characters removed. Verbatim. Never normalised.

operative_context.description: Ordered, outermost first. Order is not cosmetic: 15 U.S.C. s 1681c(a)(6)(A) needs three levels, and dropping the (a) chapeau turns an exception-to-a-prohibition into a freestanding requirement. Deliberately NOT called a stem — context can follow as well as precede.

context_not_required.description: Escape hatch for gate 18: a stated reason why a nested atom needs no context. A reason, never a boolean, so the judgement is on the record.

scope_justification.description: Required (gate 13) when subject.domain is competency-level or absent. Without it the taxonomy-as-coverage-checklist discipline erodes one reasonable exception at a time.

derived_from.description: The record this one descends from textually. Drives tools/ancestry-diff.mjs, which flags differences too small to be real legal change — punctuation-only, marker-position-only, whitespace-only, or inside a subparagraph label. Those are extraction artefacts, not amendments.

term.description: The NORMALISED concept, shared across instruments — e.g. "personal information". This is the key differs_from compares on; two records with different terms are not comparable and gate 26 will not pair them.

term_as_defined.description: The term the instrument ACTUALLY uses — "nonpublic personal information", "protected health information", "consumer report". Never normalise this: the drafter's words are the citation.

elements.description: The definition decomposed. Each element is anchored to a verbatim substring, so a concept tag can never drift away from the words that justify it.

concept.description: A key from meta/definition-concepts.yaml. Gate 26 rejects anything else — an ad-hoc concept would make two definitions look different when only the vocabulary differed.

verbatim_span.description: Quoted from the source and checked by gate 3, exactly like every other span.

condition.description: When the element applies only on stated terms — the affiliate-sharing carve-out in FCRA turns on disclosure and an opt out.

differs_from.description: COMPUTED by tools/compute-differs.mjs and re-verified by gate 26. Do not hand-edit: the gate recomputes from elements and fails on disagreement.
